title: SAML/SSO group attribute normalization causing permission flip and transient over-permission
creator: Ravi Menon
description:
Summary:
Customers reported two related but opposite permission failures after onboarding SSO group sync: (A) users intermittently saw "permission denied" for routes they should have access to; (B) other users briefly gained broader access (admin-level UI controls) during a group sync window. Affected customers include ACME Health (escalation INC-2026-0783) and two smaller customers who had recent group rename/mapping events.

This ticket tracks root-cause analysis, the cherrypicked patch, verification steps, audit-log sampling, customer communications, and follow-ups to prevent recurrence.
root_cause: Two defects combined: 1) the SSO group-name normalization function collapsed certain characters (dots, slashes) and lowercased attributes, causing distinct groups to collide (e.g., 'dev.ops' -> 'devops') which matched broader RBAC role bindings; 2) the background SSO sync job applied an in-place membership update without write-order guards, allowing a race where transient membership states were evaluated by the RBAC engine and emitted audit entries before the fully consistent mapping persisted. The RBAC v2 policy evaluator treats group allows with highest precedence for admin bindings, so collisions risked over-permission. The inverse 'permission denied' incidents occurred when the sync removed the expected attribute momentarily while the console cached previous membership leading to deny-on-read until caches invalidated.
repro_steps: 1) Configure SAML IdP to send groups with dotted names (e.g., 'team.dev.ops' and 'team.dev')
2) Enable groups -> local mapping in SSO integration and trigger a group rename/merge on the IdP side
3) Run a manual SSO sync (or wait for scheduled sync) while simultaneously opening an admin-scoped console route for a user who is member of the colliding groups

4) Observe audit logs and RBAC evaluations: first the truncated/collided group appears in membership, RBAC grants admin rights; shortly after the sync applies the full mapping which may remove the expected group causing 'permission denied' on subsequent checks
5) Confirm behavior reproduced in staging with synthetic SAML attributes and SSO sync enabled
audit_log_examples: 2026-03-11T08:23:12Z user=alice@example.com event=rbac.evaluate result=allow reason=group:devops binding=org-admin session=ae12f4
resolution_summary: Patch delivered: 1) Normalize function reverted to preserve punctuation when mapping IdP group identifiers; introduced deterministic stable-hash folding to avoid collisions instead of stripping characters. 2) SSO sync now performs atomic replace semantics for membership (compute new membership and swap in single DB transaction) and emits a single consolidated membership-change audit event. 3) RBAC evaluator enhanced with a 'sync-in-flight' guard: when a sync transaction is in progress for an org, RBAC reads prefer the pre-sync snapshot until the sync commit completes, preventing intermediate evaluation on partial state. Cherrypick PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2387. Hotfix deployed to staging 2026-03-12, canary in prod on 2026-03-13, full rollout 2026-03-14.
verification_steps: Run e2e staging scenario that previously reproduced the flip; assert no allow->deny transitions during sync window
Run audit log diff collector for a 24h window for affected orgs and verify no transient admin grants appear without corresponding stable group mappings
Ask ACME Health to validate with a controlled group rename during a maintenance window and confirm no elevated session occurred

follow_up_tasks: 1) Add integration test to CI that simulates IdP group renames with dotted/slashed names
2) Update SSO docs to recommend canonical group naming and call out reserved characters
3) Instrument metric 'sso.sync.inflight' and alert if sync duration > 30s
4) Design a migration tool to detect existing group collisions and produce a remediation plan for affected orgs
5) Schedule security walkthrough with platform customers who requested deep logs
notes: This change touches identity sync paths and RBAC evaluation; full test matrix includes: SAML, OIDC, SCIM imports, and manual console grants. We preserved backward compatibility by defaulting to the old normalization only for orgs with legacy-compat flag for 30 days; customers have been notified in the canary cohort.
